text: {"headline":"Provider 1000000034 bills 99215 well above expectation at every complexity level, including on simple acute visits, but the small set of returned charts supports the billed levels, so the pattern cannot yet be called upcoding or a sicker panel.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The billing pattern points toward upcoding: 99215 share runs roughly double the all-provider rate in every condition-count stratum, not just among complex patients, and the overall mix sits heavily at 99214. The sampled low-complexity 99215s include routine presentations such as upper respiratory infection (C0018976, C0019056, C0019300, C0020567), low back pain (C0020381, C0020582) and urinary infection (C0019003, C0020123), which rarely need high-complexity decision-making. Against this, none of the 20 documented 99215 claims was documented below the billed level. That is reassuring but weak evidence, because records cover under 2% of claims and the all-provider rate would predict only one or two mismatches in a sample that size. Some charts may also be supporting the bill on paper only: low-complexity claims C0019504 and C0020592 are documented as high MDM (C0020592 with no minutes recorded), C0018976 is flagged for a problems-list issue, some notes show repeated times, a few claim moderate-plus data review with no lab line, and no audit trail was received. A reviewer should first pull a larger, targeted chart sample of the low-complexity 99215 claims listed here, check whether their notes are templated or cloned against the presenting problem, and request the EHR audit trail."}
